lastCompletedStory.title: Make the drift guard backend-conditional and config-tolerant

nextStoryContext: isClaudeAliasModel is now exported from src/supervisor/codex-auth.ts (was module-private). The 'readPhaseModel vs repo project.toml (drift guard)' test in test/config/models.test.ts (around line 745 now) is backend-conditional: it still asserts readPhaseModel matches the configured/DEFAULTS value for every phase, but the 'known model' check now branches on readPhaseBackend(phase, repoConfigPath) -- claude-backed phases keep the MODEL_OPTIONS/DEFAULTS membership check, non-claude-backed phases only assert !isClaudeAliasModel(actual) (deliberately no positive codex-slug allowlist, since OpenAI slugs are account-specific and drift). The adjacent 'DEFAULTS vs MODEL_OPTIONS consistency' test block was untouched. scripts/cam/project.toml remains byte-unchanged (all phases still claude today, confirmed via git diff --exit-code), so the drift guard currently exercises only the claude branch in practice; the codex branch is live code but not yet hit by the repo's own config. This closes the CAM-356 epic (US-001 backend-aware readPhaseModel/readPhaseBackend, US-002 wired every dispatch site, US-003 made the drift guard tolerant of a future codex flip). A follow-up story would only be needed if project.toml is ever flipped to codex for a real phase (to confirm the non-claude branch fires as designed) or if a 7th dispatch site is added.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal test-guard + export-visibility change (isClaudeAliasModel export, drift-guard backend branching); no external library API surface was exercised.
